Zero references for IdentityProvider, InstanceSetting, and UserSetting seem suspicious. These may be storepb types rather than store.IdentityProvider. Proto store types and additional packages still need verification.

Checking whether generated proto types in proto/gen/store count as data layer entities. The store package itself defines IdentityProvider and InstanceSetting, yet external references appear to target their storepb equivalents instead.

The intended data-layer entities are likely store.User and store.Memo. User appears in 7 packages, Memo in 6. After excluding test packages, User drops to 6 and Memo to 5. Attachment ranks third with 3. Whether store/db counts as outside the layer remains unclear.

store/db is correctly excluded because it is part of the data layer. cmd/memos may reference store.Store without using entity types. Find* types are not entity types. Aliasing could hide some references. Need to verify whether storepb types such as storepb.Memo and storepb.User count toward the data layer.

User is referenced from 7 packages outside the data layer. Memo is referenced from 6. Both counts include test packages.

Reconsidering whether the data layer includes only store/db or the entire store package. If only store/db counts, all entities would be referenced equally from outside. If the whole store package counts, the current counts remain valid.

Store is the repository facade, not a persistent entity, so it is excluded. The data layer likely spans the entire store/ tree, making server, cmd, and internal the external packages. Final ranking: User (7), Memo (6).

Excluding test packages yields User (6) and Memo (5). I will list the exact package names and counts. I am also verifying that frontend/rss/auth actually reference these types.

echo "===== Memo ====="
grep -l "store.Memo" --include="*.go" /bench/repo/server /bench/repo/cmd /bench/repo/internal -r 2>/dev/null | grep -v "/store/"
echo "===== Attachment ====="
grep -l "store.Attachment" --include="*.go" /bench/repo/server /bench/repo/cmd /bench/repo/internal -r 2>/dev/null | grep -v "/store/"
echo "===== packages for User (unique dirs) ====="
grep -rl "store.User\b" --include="*.go" /bench/repo --exclude-dir=web --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=proto --exclude-dir=store | sed 's|/[^/]*$||' | sort -u
echo "===== packages for Memo ====="
grep -rl "store.Memo\b" --include="*.go" /bench/repo --exclude-dir=web --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=proto --exclude-dir=store | sed 's|/[^/]*$||' | sort -u

message.text:
Grep indicates fileserver.go references store.Memo, yet the Memo package list omits it. This discrepancy needs resolution before ranking entity usage.

The word-boundary grep correctly excludes fileserver from the Memo package list. frontend_test.go references User and Memo from within the frontend package.

User is referenced by 7 packages. Memo is referenced by 6 packages. These are the top two persistent entity types.

h11.
1st: User (~7 packages); 2nd: Memo (~6 packages)

Persistent entities live in `store/` (`User`, `Memo`, `Attachment`, and so on). Outside that tree, `store.User` appears in `server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/frontend`, and `server/router/rss`. `store.Memo` appears in `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`, and `server/runner/memopayload`. Next is `Attachment` (~4). Excluding the test package, User is still first (~6) and Memo second (~5).
